explanation: Modern C++ introduces smart pointers as a safer and more expressive alternative to raw pointers for resource management. They automate memory management through RAII (Resource Acquisition Is Initialization), ensuring proper deallocation and preventing common issues like memory leaks and dangling pointers. Smart pointers such as std::unique_ptr, std::shared_ptr, and std::weak_ptr enable clear ownership semantics and facilitate exception-safe code, making resource management explicit and less error-prone in C++ programming.
syntax:
std::unique_ptr<Type> ptr = std::make_unique<Type>(constructor_args); // exclusive ownership
std::shared_ptr<Type> ptr1 = std::make_shared<Type>(constructor_args); // shared ownership
std::weak_ptr<Type> weakPtr = ptr1; // non-owning reference to shared object
example_explanation: This example demonstrates the use of modern C++ smart pointers to manage resource lifetime safely. The std::unique_ptr ensures exclusive ownership of a Resource object, automatically destroying it when it goes out of scope. The std::shared_ptr allows multiple owners, with the resource being destroyed only when the last shared_ptr is destroyed. The std::weak_ptr provides a non-owning reference, which can be used to observe the resource without affecting its lifetime. This exemplifies modern C++ idioms for resource management, reducing the risk of memory leaks and dangling pointers.
